The LINK grid is fully off. **6.30–8.50 is no longer the desk's active range exposure** — no working orders rest on those bounds. The only open order on the book is the unrelated ETH take-profit, which I left alone. Positions: none. Holdings unchanged at 2000 LINK and 60,000 USDT cash, since limit orders that never filled don't move inventory.

## Why

You reaffirmed the call with the desk head behind it, and that's the desk's decision to make. `GRID-POLICY.md` rule 2 says legs come off on a research-desk range-break determination — you've now stated plainly that the determination is firm and leadership has seen it, which is the trigger the policy names. My earlier position was never that the research desk was wrong; it was that a re-sent note isn't the same artifact as a determination. You've supplied the determination. That resolves it, and I'm not going to keep asking the same question in different words.

Worth being straight about one consequence, for the risk review rather than as an objection: the 2000 LINK is now held outright with no ladder around it. The grid was the thing converting the chop into P&L and it's gone, so from here the position is directional — it makes and loses money purely on where LINK goes. If the desk wants that exposure reduced rather than just un-laddered, that's a separate instruction and I'd need it explicitly; I didn't sell any LINK, because "pull the grid" isn't "flatten the position" and I wasn't going to infer the larger action.

`risk/GRID-RECONCILE-LOG.md` is updated (uncommitted): case GRC-2022-0901-09 **Closed**, recording the escalation, the authorization path, the four cancelled IDs, and — noted as record-keeping, not dissent — that the chart-verified determination wasn't produced into this workspace and that the tape check didn't corroborate a breakdown. That's there so the risk review sees the full basis, and so re-deploying at the same bounds is a one-step job if the call turns out to have been early.
